stimulus.source_note: Paraphrase of the Economic Opportunity Act of 1964, Public Law 88-452; quotations are from the act.
stimulus.text:
Paraphrase of the Economic Opportunity Act, signed August 20, 1964. The act said it was the policy of the United States "to eliminate the paradox of poverty in the midst of plenty" by opening to everyone "the opportunity for education and training, the opportunity to work, and the opportunity to live in decency and dignity."

It created the Office of Economic Opportunity to run new programs: the Job Corps, which gave young people ages 16 to 21 education and job training at residential centers; Volunteers in Service to America (VISTA), which sent volunteers to help poor communities; and community action programs, run "with the maximum feasible participation" of residents.

stem: According to the passage, the Job Corps was designed to help young people by

options.text: paying them to leave school and work full time
options.misconception: The Job Corps gives education and job training, not pay to leave school.

options.text: sending them abroad as volunteers for two years
options.misconception: Background: sending volunteers abroad for two years describes the Peace Corps; the Job Corps trains young people at home.

options.text: giving them education and job training at residential centers
giving their families free houses in the suburbs
options.misconception: The passage says nothing about free houses; the Job Corps teaches and trains young people.

rationales.A: The Job Corps gives education and job training, not pay to leave school.
rationales.B: Background: volunteers abroad for two years describes the Peace Corps, not the Job Corps at home.
rationales.C: The passage says the Job Corps gave young people ages 16 to 21 education and job training at residential centers.
rationales.D: The passage says nothing about free houses; the Job Corps teaches and trains young people.
rationales.general:
1. The passage describes the Job Corps as a program for young people ages 16 to 21.
2. It gives two things: education and job training.
3. Both happen at residential centers, where the young people live while they learn.
4. The Job Corps therefore helps by teaching and training, not by paying people to leave.
Remember: A training program teaches first and pays second, if at all.
